bundles.title: Governor: adaptive slot control and free-memory gate
bundles.description:
Improve the board slot governor that LMW-4 installed (PR #72 and its fix; log at ~/.multica-codex/board-governor.jsonl). Keep it small and extend the existing governor; do not add a second one.

1. Adaptive limit (AIMD, as in Netflix concurrency-limits): grow the slot count by one at a time only after a sustained healthy window (load per core, memory pressure, swap and compressor growth, board response time all good), and cut it multiplicatively on pressure (for example halve on high disk wait or memory pressure, to zero on emergency). Replace fixed thresholds where they cause the limit to stick, such as the current hold at 7 with reason pressure_or_reserve while load is around 8 on 14 cores.
2. Start gate (as in GNU parallel --memfree and make -l): before the board starts a new agent, require free memory above a floor plus the per-agent cost (about 2 GB and 0.8 cores from the live readings), and load below a ceiling; otherwise the task stays queued.
3. Waiting agents: make the explicit-wait path the default for long waits (waiting on another task, a PR merge, a deploy window, a reset), so waiting agents release their slot. Document how an agent should wait in the wiki how-to and worker instructions.
4. Read the AGPL-free ideas only; do not copy code from Netflix concurrency-limits or other projects.

Prove it on the live board: a log excerpt showing the limit rising one slot at a time after a healthy window, falling on a real or simulated pressure spike, a start held back by the memory gate, and a waiting agent releasing its slot so a queued task starts. Install without interrupting running agent sessions.

## Safety first (Shyam, 2026-10-27 02:00 UTC)
The governor should flex the slot count on the fly, but it must never let the Mac overload. Tonight it raised slots to 9 while the load average was 194 (reason 'sustained_load'), earlier raised 7 to 8 under 'emergency_pressure_incomplete', and the Mac had to be force-restarted after CPU and memory hit 100%. The Coordinator has paused it (launchctl bootout of ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.shyam.board-governor.plist) and set board.agents to 4 by hand.
Hard rules:
- It may never raise the limit while any pressure signal is bad (load per core, memory pressure, swap or compressor growth, disk wait, board response time), and any error, timeout or missing reading means hold or lower, never raise.
- On critical pressure it lowers immediately and also acts on running work (pause or stop the newest heavy jobs) instead of only blocking new starts; coordinate with LMW-7's backstop so there is one mechanism, not two.
- It never sets the limit above a ceiling derived from cores and memory, and never above what the last healthy window supports.
Prove it before turning it back on: replay tonight's real readings from ~/.multica-codex/board-governor.jsonl (load 117 to 361) and show it would have lowered every time; run a controlled stress test that pushes load and memory up and show it pulls back before the Mac is unresponsive; then re-enable it with launchctl bootstrap and show a live log of it raising one slot at a time when healthy.

## Priority and deadlines (Shyam, 2026-10-27 02:40 UTC)
Tonight the order of work depended on the Coordinator stopping and re-delegating tasks by hand to move the critical one forward, and the deploy for the 13:30 UTC open waited about 6 hours across two restarts.
- Priority: support a per-task priority (and an optional deadline) so open-critical work starts first; check first whether the board already has a priority or ordering setting, and use it instead of building one. If the board needs a change, write the upstream issue or PR text for eliasstravik/herdr-projects; do not patch the installed plugin.
- Reserved slot: keep one slot for the highest-priority task whenever it is ready, so it never waits behind lower-priority work.
- Cap on running work: when the limit drops below the number of running agents, pause the lowest-priority heavy agents first (keep their work), instead of only blocking new starts.
- Wait visibility: log each task's wait time and cause (slot, review, merge, dependency, human) so the Coordinator can report the longest wait and its deadline every 15 minutes.
Prove it on the live board: a high-priority task added behind four queued ones starts first, and a cap drop pauses the lowest-priority heavy agent.

## Bug found (2026-10-27 03:50 UTC)
The explicit wait does not work from a board agent: SRW-41 ran 'herdr-projects wait SRW-41 --until ... --reason ...' (and with SRW-41) and got exit 1, 'wait can only be used by SRW41 own agent', from inside its own board session. So agents cannot release a slot while waiting and fall back to ending their turn or polling. Fix or work around this (find how the board identifies the owning agent, for example an environment variable missing from codex sessions), and prove a real board agent can wait and give its slot to a queued task. Also: a task whose agent process is gone must not keep its slot (LMW-4's dead session held one for about 3 hours).

## Next steps (Coordinator, 2026-10-27 15:45 UTC; restarted on Claude after a stuck Cursor message)
1. Put main's load backstop back live: the running copy differs from main (it adds REQUEST_TTL_SECONDS and request-curtail handling, unmerged). Run main's load_backstop.py install then resume (LMW-14's backup is ~/.multica-codex/load-backstop.backup-20261027T074117), keep agents alive, confirm with cmp against main. Install new versions only after their PR merges; add the main-only install check you started.
2. Recalibrate the memory gate: today tasks idled on 'memory pressure' while 43 to 46 percent of memory was free and load was 6 to 8. Base the gate on free memory, swap growth and load per core, not the macOS pressure level alone. Pass test: no task waits on memory while more than 30 percent is free, and the replay of the overnight overload still throttles every time.
3. Fix the remaining review findings, prove live safety, then turn the governor on and end your turn.

## Hand off now (Coordinator, 17:10 UTC; restarted on pi after a stuck omp message)
The priority memory-gate fix is committed (2afc936) and the premature-resume fix (4d5eede); the closing note is written. Check the branch is pushed and the replay proof still passes on current main, then end your turn so the board reviews and merges it. Do not start new work in this round.

## Scope for this task (Coordinator, 2026-10-27 20:10 UTC; replaces the proof list above)
Seven reviews failed on two things this task cannot do from llmwiki: (a) an atomic memory and load gate inside the board's own start and wake path, which is upstream issue eliasstravik/herdr-projects#418, and (b) live acceptance, which needs the governor installed from merged main. Both move out of this task.
Done for this task: the governor code, the replay of the overnight overload (every reading lowers or holds), the critical-pressure curtail through LMW-7's backstop, and the bounded stress test, merged with the governor left turned off. The closing note lists the open live checks and links #418. Live acceptance is a separate follow-up after this merges.

bundles.description:
Verification is the SRW bottleneck (Shyam, 2026-10-28: 'why is verification taking so long'). Facts from 2026-10-27/28: one full run of test_srw16_release_gate.js took 1303 s (about 22 min) on SRW-68; each task runs it several times (the agent's own run, the board check, again after every review round, again after every rebase when another task merges, and again in the deploy task); heavy runs 2 to 4 jobs at a time, and today it curtailed SRW jobs 15 times and paused them 9 times on load.

Goal: a task's gate costs minutes, not an hour, without weakening what it checks.
1. Profile the gate: time per step (index-lotto, copy-trading, real-corpus, reject-all, feature gate, and the rest) over three runs; find what dominates and why (serial replay, repeated setup, cold dependency installs, sleeps or polling).
2. Speed it up: parallelise independent steps inside one heavy admission within the CPU budget heavy grants, reuse setup, and keep the full real-post corpus replay. Consider 5 variations and pick by measured time.
3. Run once per commit: write a gate receipt keyed by the commit SHA (and Node version and lockfile hash); the board check, the reviewer and the deploy automation reuse a passing receipt for the same SHA instead of rerunning. Any change to the commit means a new run.
4. Keep every existing assertion; a deliberately broken commit must still fail.
Proof: before and after timings for each step and in total (target: total under 8 minutes on this Mac under heavy), a negative control that still fails, the board check reusing a receipt for an unchanged SHA, and the gate passing through ~/.local/bin/heavy. This task is the only one allowed to change test_srw16_release_gate.js and its runner; other tasks keep running it unchanged.

bundles.description:
Keep this repo's state charts and formal verification current, find real bugs, and fix them.

1. State charts: load the statechart and state-machine-thinking skills. For every entity in this repo with a status, lifecycle, queue, retry loop or concurrent state change (orders and positions, jobs, syncs, deploys, sessions, approvals and the like), keep a state chart in docs/state-charts/ (one file per machine, Mermaid stateDiagram plus a short table of states, events, guards and side effects), linked from the repo docs index. Create the folder and index on the first run; on later runs, update only the charts whose code changed since the last run (git log since the previous chart commit) and add charts for new machines.
2. Formal verification: for the highest-risk machine that does not yet have a current spec, use /create-formal-verification-skill (and /maintain-formal-verification-skill for existing specs) as described in /Users/shyamsivakumar/Code/llmwiki/source/docs/how-to/formal-verification-with-tla.md. Model the real code paths, state the safety invariants (for example no double order, no trade from an unconsumed condition, no lost state on restart) and liveness properties, and run the model checker through heavy.
3. Bugs: every counterexample must be reproduced against the real code (a replay, a script on real data, or the existing test suite), never assumed. Fix each confirmed bug in this task, extending the existing owners; no new unit test files. Record unconfirmed or out-of-scope findings in the closing note.
4. Report: list the charts added or updated, specs added or updated with their invariants, model-checker results, bugs confirmed and fixed (with file:line and proof), and what the next run should cover.
Guardrails: one heavy command at a time through heavy; stop if load per core reaches 1; paper only for trading code; never deploy or change production from this task.
